title: I love raiding in Rust, but I don’t want to spend days getting there — so I made my own game
author: Bottle_777
selftext:
**RaidMade** — a smaller, simpler game focused almost entirely on the fun part: preparing a raid, figuring out the best way in, blowing through walls and doors, grabbing the loot, and preparing for the next target.

It started as a small prototype, but I ended up adding different raid targets, destructible structures, tools and explosives, resource processing, progression, and a bunch of smaller systems around the core loop.

I still haven’t written any code manually — the whole game was built through prompting Codex, mostly Luna XHigh, then constantly playtesting and iterating on the result.

**Playable link:** [https://wandering-frog-b1e4.quietforge.workers.dev/](https://wandering-frog-b1e4.quietforge.workers.dev/)

Would love to hear whether the raiding itself feels satisfying and whether you actually want to go for another raid afterward.

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: Looks very good chests should be 3d.

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
Yeah, making them fully 3D would make sense considering how central they are to the game, but that’s also part of the limitation of the visual style I chose.

A billboard effect probably wouldn’t work here because placing the chests involves rotating them.

I’ll think about a cleaner solution.

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: Three.js with vanilla JavaScript, HTML/CSS, and WebGL — no game engine.

comments.author: Commando501
comments.body:
I see your work and all I can think of is turning this into a RuneScape hardcore survival RPG game. 

I like the work you've done brother!

replies.body: Glad you liked it! Yeah, the atmosphere ended up feeling pretty distinctive — I could definitely see something harsher and more hardcore being built on top of it.
